mechanism_narrative: The sharp week-0 drop in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES marks an abrupt collapse in commuting and shared travel, which will depress discretionary retail visits within 1-2 weeks and keep RETAIL_REC below its prior 4-week average over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:week-0 TRANSIT fell from 11.4 to -2.0 and WORKPLACES from 9.9 to -1.7
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises above the prior 4-week mean while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain depressed for two consecutive weeks, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL turns positive after several negative weeks, time spent at home displaces shopping trips and suppresses retail footfall over the next 4 weeks, especially if transit mobility is simultaneously falling.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL crosses from negative to positive week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL moved from -1.7 to 2.0 at week-0 while TRANSIT moved from 11.4 to -2.0
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the prior 4-week mean after RESIDENTIAL turns positive, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained surge in GROCERY_PHARM indicates stock-up and essential-trip behavior that substitutes for discretionary shopping; after a one-week lag, RETAIL_REC should weaken as households concentrate trips on essentials.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM jumped from 11.0 to 18.4 in the latest week
failure_condition: If retail mobility stays flat or increases while grocery/pharmacy mobility remains elevated for two weeks, the claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT falls below zero, the city is likely in a restriction regime that reduces spontaneous shopping trips; that regime will pull RETAIL_REC down over the next 4 weeks even if grocery activity stays high.
evidence_refs: fact:week-0 TRANSIT is -2.0 while GROCERY_PHARM is 18.4
failure_condition: If TRANSIT remains negative but RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week average, the restriction channel is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A brief spike in PARKS mobility signals weather or calendar-driven outdoor substitution; when park visits jump, some discretionary outings are diverted away from indoor retail, lowering RETAIL_REC over the following 2 weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from 0.6 to 8.1 in the latest week
failure_condition: If a parks spike is followed by no drop in RETAIL_REC within two weeks, the seasonal substitution mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent weakness in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT over a full month implies fewer commuter-linked retail trips; RETAIL_REC should therefore remain below the prior four-week mean over the next 4 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both series turned negative at week-0
failure_condition: If retail mobility recovers despite continued low workplace and transit mobility for four weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rising GROCERY_PHARM series followed by a falling PARKS series indicates a shift from outdoor and discretionary movement toward short essential trips, which should pressure RETAIL_REC down within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises while PARKS falls in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose to 18.4 while PARKS remained volatile
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not weaken in the week after grocery rises and parks falls together, this interaction is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Under tightening restrictions, the combined break in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility is the leading signal of reduced retail access; once both series are negative, RETAIL_REC should trend lower for the next month.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are below 0
evidence_refs: fact:week-0 both series are negative after earlier positive readings
failure_condition: If both series remain below zero but retail mobility stabilizes or increases over four weeks, the mechanism is rejected.
